key_insight: A simple online monitor can make LLM deployment safer by converting an external verifier’s signal into real-time alarms. With threshold calibration via risk control, this lightweight approach performs competitively on reasoning and red-teaming tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to detect unsafe LLM outputs during deployment, when alignment training alone is not enough and risky generations can still occur.
method: Use an external verifier model to score each LLM output in real time.
Convert the verifier score into an alarm decision by applying a threshold.
Calibrate the threshold with risk-control methods so the monitor meets a target safety risk.
Evaluate the monitor on mathematical reasoning and red-teaming datasets to test detection performance.
impact: This gives practitioners a practical safety layer that can be added at deployment time without changing the base model. It helps teams decide when to trust an LLM output and when to escalate, block, or review.

paper_authors: Mona Schirmer, Metod Jazbec, Alexander Timans, Christian Naesseth, Maja Waldron
